findings: The limiter keys buckets by `req.ip`, not by API key as the documentation claims ("Each API key is limited to 100 requests per minute"); customers behind a shared office IP/NAT collapse into a single bucket and share one 100-request allowance across all their API keys, directly explaining why the customer is rate-limited far more easily than the docs suggest.

`checkLimit` has no time-window logic at all — the count is only ever incremented (`(buckets.get(key) || 0) + 1`) and never reset or expired — so the documented "100 requests per minute" is actually enforced as a single lifetime cap of 100 requests, not a rolling per-minute limit.

Because there is no reset, once a bucket's count passes 100 it can never recover: every future request from that key/IP returns `limited: true` permanently (until process restart), contradicting the "per minute" framing that implies the limit clears over time.

The documentation states exceeding the limit "returns HTTP 429 ... with a Retry-After header indicating when to retry," but `checkLimit` only returns `{ limited: boolean }` — it never computes a retry time, never builds a 429 response, and never sets any header, so the documented Retry-After behavior is not implemented anywhere in this code.

The `buckets` Map has no eviction, TTL, or cleanup logic for any key, so it accumulates entries and grows unboundedly for the life of the process — a direct consequence of the missing reset/window logic noted above.
